name: key-value
summary: The DS key-value / description list (obs-key-value) — the product's column-grid-view / overview-layout: a TRANSPOSED grid where columns become row labels (a tinted label cell) + the record's value. A single-record DETAIL view, common in widget overviews and detail panels. NOT a data table (it only shares the grid chrome) — for rows-of-records use obs-table.
element_note: Split out of the Storybook Table 'key-value (transposed)' variant — it's a detail LAYOUT, not a data table.

variants.name: card
variants.what: default — bordered card with a tinted label cell (column-grid-view)

variants.name: two-column
variants.what: [element] columns="2" — pairs laid out two-across (overview-layout 2-columns) for wide records

variants.name: color-coded
variants.what: [element] a value coloured by a --severity token (item's 3rd field / `color` key) — the product ColorCodedCell colouring

variants.name: status
variants.what: [element] a value rendered as an obs-tag (item's 4th field / `status` key) — the overview-layout status cell

items.note: [[label, value], …] or [[label, value, color, status], …] or [{label, value, color?, status?}] — JSON string or a JS array. `color` is a --severity token that colours the value; `status` (e.g. "running") renders the value as an obs-tag.

variant.note: [element] card (bordered card, tinted label — column-grid-view) | plain (borderless, muted label — overview-layout)

columns.note: [element] 1 | 2 — pairs per row (columns=2 lays the pairs out two-across, the overview-layout 2-columns layout)

decisionFlow: Showing ONE record's fields as label→value pairs (a detail / overview panel)? -> Key-Value.
Rows of MANY records with columns? -> the Table (obs-table).
Headline metrics (big number + unit)? -> Metric List (obs-metric-list).
do: Use for a record's detail/overview (label | value).
Keep labels short; the label cell is tinted (card variant).
Use columns="2" for many fields; colour a threshold value with a --severity token; render a status value as a tag via `status`.
dont: Don't use for tabular records (use obs-table).
Don't use for KPI metrics (use obs-metric-list).
Don't hardcode a value colour — use a --severity token; don't use 2 columns for long-wrapping values.

key-value.useWhen: a single record's fields shown as label→value pairs (detail / overview panel)
key-value.dontUse: for tabular records (obs-table) or headline metrics (obs-metric-list)
key-value.example: a monitor detail panel: Monitor: web-server-01, IP: 10.0.0.12, Type: Linux Server, Uptime: 42 days

card.useWhen: the default — a bordered card with a tinted label cell, for a self-contained detail panel/widget
card.dontUse: when the pairs sit inside an already-bordered container or a dense inline overview — use `plain`
card.example: a monitor detail card in a drawer or overview widget

plain.useWhen: an inline, borderless detail with muted labels (the overview-layout style) — inside another card/section
plain.dontUse: when the block needs its own visual boundary — use `card`
plain.example: a properties block inside a larger detail page section

two-column.useWhen: a record has MANY fields — columns="2" lays the pairs two-across so it reads compactly (overview-layout 2-columns)
two-column.dontUse: for a few pairs (1 column is cleaner) or when values are long and would wrap
two-column.example: an asset inventory panel: Vendor / Model / Uptime / OS / Site / Rack across two columns

color-coded.useWhen: a value signals severity/threshold state — pass a `color` (a --severity token) as the item's 3rd field / key
color-coded.dontUse: don't hardcode a hex; don't colour a value with no threshold meaning

status.useWhen: a value IS a status — pass `status` (e.g. "running"/"down") as the 4th field / key to render it as an obs-tag
status.dontUse: for plain text values (leave status empty); for a big KPI number use obs-metric-list
status.example: Status: a green Running obs-tag inside the detail panel

a11y.summary: Semantically a description list — prefer a <dl> if possible; the label cell should be associated with its value. Ensure sufficient contrast on the tinted label cell.

knownIssues: [element] obs-key-value is FUNCTIONAL: pass items ([label,value] pairs/objects). Split from the Storybook Table 'key-value (transposed)' variant since it's a detail layout, not a data table.
changelog: 2026-07-13: dark-mode label fix (owner) — the card label cell used --neutral-dark, which resolves near-black (#172336) in dark mode → invisible on the dark tinted label cell. Switched to --neutral-regular (muted in both themes: light #7186a8 / dark #6a7fa0). Readable in both.

2026-07-13: variants + playground (owner) — added `variant` (card [default, tinted card] | plain [borderless, muted — overview-layout]), `columns` (1 | 2 — pairs two-across, overview-layout 2-columns), color-coded values (a --severity token as the item's 3rd field), and status values (a 4th field renders the value as an obs-tag). Added the Details-tab playground (variant + columns selects + dataset presets) and gallery examples. Documented the full surface in the new prose spec.

2026-07-13: row hover (owner) — added a real row-hover highlight on the value cell (`tr:hover td.val` → --neutral-lighter, 0.12s ease; the tinted label cell stays put). Earlier this was wrongly dismissed as an Inspect-mode artifact; the owner wanted an actual hover affordance.

2026-07-13: width fix (owner) — the playground was shrink-wrapping the widget to ~208px (labels wrapped); changed :host to display:block, widened the max-width, and gave the element full stage width so labels/values sit on one line.
2026-07-13: shipped <obs-key-value> — the DS key-value / description list (column-grid-view / overview-layout). Split out of the Storybook Table variant set (it's a detail LAYOUT, not a table).
